data.content:
Not valid. The premise—that a per-item error still lands in `onSuccess`—doesn't hold for this batch mechanism.

Looking at [batch.ts](src/Utils/request/batch.ts):

1. **The batch is atomic.** Per the backend contract documented in the hook: "The backend runs all the given requests in series in one atomic transaction. If one request fails, the backend rolls back all the changes and gives a 4xx/5xx status for the full batch."

2. **A per-item failure throws, so `onSuccess` never runs.** In `mutationFn`, when the batch returns a non-2xx (because a sub-request failed), the caught `HTTPError` is re-thrown:
   ```ts
   throw new HTTPError({ message: "Batch Request Failed", status: error.status, silent: true, cause: error.cause });
   ```
   That routes to `onError`/`onSettled`, not `onSuccess`. `onSuccess` fires **only** when the whole batch is 2xx, i.e., every sub-request succeeded.

3. **So `results` in `onSuccess` is always the all-succeeded set.** The `.some(r => r.reference_id === "upsert-observations")` check isn't testing success — it's testing *whether the observations request was part of the batch at all*. That request is added conditionally:
   ```ts
   if (formattedObservations.length > 0) {
     requests.push({ ..., referenceId: "upsert-observations", ... });
   }
   ```
   The report-update request (`"update-report"`) is always present. So the `.some(...)` is just distinguishing "we actually saved observations" (→ "test results saved") from "we only updated the report/conclusion" — and correctly showing the toast only in the former case.

So there's no path where a failed sub-item produces a "saved successfully" toast. The comment misreads the atomic-batch semantics. The only thing you'd correctly note is that `results` here is guaranteed successful, so an explicit status check would be redundant.
data.reasoningText:
I'm seeing how the batch transaction works — the backend treats the entire batch as a single atomic operation, so if any sub-request fails, the whole batch returns a 4xx/5xx status. When that happens in the `mutationFn`, it re-throws the HTTPError, which means `onError` gets called instead of `onSuccess`. The `onSuccess` callback only fires when the batch completes successfully.

So the comment claiming "per-item errors still trigger the success toast" is incorrect. The `.some()` check isn't validating whether individual requests succeeded — it's just checking whether the observations upsert was included in the batch at all. Since `onSuccess` only runs on full batch success, all results are guaranteed to have succeeded already.
